niche.habitat: Hydrothermal plumes and active chimney surfaces at fluid-rock interfaces
niche.diet: Chemo-electric; oxidizes H2 and reduces Fe2+ while harvesting electrical current from mechanical strain on piezoelectric crystals

body: Asymmetric tangle of black, tensile filaments embedded with magnetite crystals, reinforced by gas-filled vesicles

links: Hydrothermal vents leach dissolved iron and sulfides from crustal rock
Rapid cooling in fluid plumes precipitates iron as magnetite microcrystals
Organisms secrete protein scaffolds that align magnetite into load-bearing arrays
Result: Filaments achieve structural integrity against 1.53g gravity and acquire piezoelectric response

skill.effect: Locks filaments into a rigid, magnetized shield; absorbs 40% of incoming kinetic damage and reflects acoustic pulses.

chains.weakness: Filaments are brittle to resonant frequencies; matching the vent's dominant vibration shatters the crystal arrays.
observe: Filaments shimmer with a metallic sheen in bioluminescence
Joints crackle with static when the wind shifts
No mouth; filaments feed directly from the flow

journal.en: It wears the mountain's blood as armor.

plausibility.summary: Scaffold magnetite/maghemite for tensile armor and magnetism; add vent-precipitated silica (quartz) nanocrystals or collagen-like biopolymer in the matrix for piezoelectric coupling. Rename diet hook to chemolithotrophy with optional strain sensing, not magnetite-as-piezo.
fixes: Scaffold magnetite/maghemite for tensile armor and magnetism; add vent-precipitated silica (quartz) nanocrystals or collagen-like biopolymer in the matrix for piezoelectric coupling. Rename diet hook to chemolithotrophy with optional strain sensing, not magnetite-as-piezo.

analogues.organism: Iron-oxidizing bacteria mineral sheaths and stalks; magnetotactic bacteria (magnetite magnetosomes, e.g. Magnetospirillum).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

links: Vent plumes release heat and chemicals in turbulent, oscillating bursts
Turbulence exerts oscillating drag forces on suspended filaments
Natural selection favors filaments tuned to the plume's resonant frequency
Resonant vibration strains embedded magnetite crystals, generating piezoelectric voltage

skill.effect: Amplifies filament vibration to emit a focused 5 kHz pulse; deals 25 damage and stuns acoustic-based foes for 2 turns.

chains.weakness: Silence is lethal; in still water, it cannot generate power and suffers 15% max HP per turn.
observe: Filaments hum and glow faintly during vent surges
Sparks jump between adjacent crystal clusters
Movement is minimal; the creature vibrates in place

journal.en: It doesn't eat; it plays the mountain until the mountain feeds it.

plausibility.summary: Primary metabolism: hydrogenotrophic and/or Fe-oxidizing chemolithotrophy on filaments; piezoelectric strain as trigger for ion flux, symbiont exchange, or small supplementary ATP. Weakness: still flow cuts chemosynthesis and sensory lock, not 15% HP/turn from piezo starvation alone.
fixes: Primary metabolism: hydrogenotrophic and/or Fe-oxidizing chemolithotrophy on filaments; piezoelectric strain as trigger for ion flux, symbiont exchange, or small supplementary ATP. Weakness: still flow cuts chemosynthesis and sensory lock, not 15% HP/turn from piezo starvation alone.

analogues.organism: Vent methanotrophs and hydrogenotrophs (chemoautotrophy); bone/collagen piezoelectricity in remodeling (Fukada-style), not primary production.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Surface pressure is 12 bar dominated by H2 with trace He/CH4
Dense hydrogen gas and fluid transmit acoustic waves at ~1200 m/s with low attenuation
Low-frequency vibrations travel vast distances without dissipation
Sensory pits along filaments detect interference patterns in the pressure field
Creature maps predators, vents, and mates via acoustic tomography

skill.effect: Reveals all units within 50m on the grid and grants +20% accuracy to ranged attacks.

chains.weakness: Cannot detect silent movers (stealth skills) or creatures insulated from vibration (heavy armor/insulation).
observe: Filaments twitch instantly to distant impacts
Creature ignores visual stimuli but locks onto sound

journal.en: In the dark, it sees the shape of sound.

plausibility.summary: Map vent field via low-frequency particle motion in chimney throats and along crack networks; game 50 m matches plausible vent-edge sensing. Drop kilometer claim or restrict it to rare ice-fracture or basin-scale paths with narrowband hums in quiet water.
fixes: Map vent field via low-frequency particle motion in chimney throats and along crack networks; game 50 m matches plausible vent-edge sensing. Drop kilometer claim or restrict it to rare ice-fracture or basin-scale paths with narrowband hums in quiet water.

analogues.organism: Fish lateral line; cephalopod and crustacean statocysts; elephant low-frequency seismic communication over long ground paths (from memory, unverified for vent noise).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Atmospheric H2 partial pressure is ~11 bar
H2 diffuses readily into hydrophobic biological vesicles
High gravity (1.53g) demands dense support, but H2 bladders provide buoyancy
Bladders allow suspension in high-velocity plumes without sinking or dragging
Buoyancy positions filaments optimally in chemical gradients

skill.effect: Adjusts bladder volume to move 10m instantly without action cost; grants advantage on next evasion check.

chains.weakness: Rapid depressurization causes vesicle rupture; takes 30 damage if exposed to low-pressure zones.
observe: Glowing gas pockets pulse rhythmically within filaments
Creature drifts upward when flow ceases
Skin feels spongy but resilient under pressure

journal.en: It breathes the sky to dance on the water.

plausibility.summary: Gas vesicles only in low-pressure chimney or plume zones above the benthos, or pressure-compensated lipid-dominated vacuoles plus rheophilic tethering in flow. Buoyant Shift as micro-lift in vent updraft, not neutral buoyancy at 250 MPa. Weakness: violent decompression or breach of high-pressure vesicles, not generic low-pressure surface exposure unless the creature is carried up a chimney.
fixes: Gas vesicles only in low-pressure chimney or plume zones above the benthos, or pressure-compensated lipid-dominated vacuoles plus rheophilic tethering in flow. Buoyant Shift as micro-lift in vent updraft, not neutral buoyancy at 250 MPa. Weakness: violent decompression or breach of high-pressure vesicles, not generic low-pressure surface exposure unless the creature is carried up a chimney.

analogues.organism: Fish swim bladder (O2/N2); some deep taxa use lipid floatation instead of gas at depth (from memory, unverified).

relations.note: (council kind 'predator') Silt-Crawlers ignore Cuerda de Hierro, mistaking the vibrating filaments for inert rock; the creature benefits from this camouflage.
(council kind 'commensal') Vent-Limpets graze on bacteria that colonize the Cuerda's filaments; the Cuerda tolerates this as the grazing stimulates flow.

temperament: Resonant, defensive, symbiotic with vent flow; highly sensitive to vibration
secrets: Tuning a skill to the creature's resonant frequency calms it and reveals a vent cache rich in rare minerals.
Its magnetite crystals can be harvested to craft gear with unique acoustic properties.
A dried specimen, if placed near a vent, will slowly rehydrate and resume vibrating, acting as a perpetual warning beacon.
moments: You approach a 'rock formation' near a vent. The filaments are so still they look like mineral deposits. When you step on a loose stone, the Cuerda wakes. It doesn't attack you; it latches onto your tool, harvests the kinetic energy of your movement, and glows brighter. You realize the 'monster' is just a harp string, and you've been strumming it.

journal.en: It doesn't eat food; it eats gravity's song.
The iron in its veins remembers every eruption.
